question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

She was amazed by / the unique architecture of / the Sydney Opera House.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "She was amazed by the unique architecture of the Sydney Opera House" is grammatically complete and correct.

◦ The passive structure "was amazed by" is correct (we are amazed by something).

◦ "the unique architecture of the Sydney Opera House" uses the right preposition "of" to show possession/relationship.

• There is no error of tense, article, preposition or agreement in any segment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Amazed" is a participial adjective describing a feeling; it is followed by "by/at". (चकित / आश्चर्यचकित)

• "Unique" already means "one of a kind", so it is used with the definite article "the architecture" here correctly.

NOTE

• In error-detection questions, first check tense, subject–verb agreement, articles, prepositions and word order. If every part is correct, the answer is "No error".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He told / his senior, "I / will sung a song / at the party tonight."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. will sung a song.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the modal auxiliary "will", the base form (V1) of the verb must be used, not the past participle. So it should be "will sing a song", not "will sung a song".

◦ Correct: He told his senior, "I will sing a song at the party tonight."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The verb "sing" is conjugated: sing – sang – sung (V1 – V2 – V3). "Sung" (V3) is used only with "have/has/had" or in the passive, never after "will".

NOTE

• Rule: Modal (will, shall, can, may, must, should) + V1 (base form). E.g., "will go", "can play", "must finish".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

There was no one left in the world whom they could call _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. theirs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a possessive pronoun that stands alone (nothing follows it). That word is "theirs" — meaning "belonging to them".

◦ Correct: There was no one left in the world whom they could call theirs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "there's" = there is (a contraction), which makes no sense here.

• "their's" is always wrong — possessive pronouns never take an apostrophe.

• "their" is a possessive adjective and must be followed by a noun (their book), so it cannot end the sentence.

NOTE

• Possessive pronouns take no apostrophe: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs, its. Only nouns use 's for possession.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Exemplary
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Excellent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Exemplary" means serving as a desirable model; very good; outstanding. Its closest synonym is "excellent". (अनुकरणीय / उत्कृष्ट)

◦ Example: The soldier received an award for his exemplary courage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Bad", Option 2 "Ordinary" and Option 4 "Average" are antonyms of exemplary.

NOTE

• Synonyms of exemplary: excellent, admirable, commendable, praiseworthy, model. Antonyms: ordinary, average, poor, unworthy.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and complete the expression.

I begin to pronounce the sequence of words and numbers that will prevent her from giving him a piece of her ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. mind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to give someone a piece of one's mind" means to scold or angrily tell someone what you really think of them. (किसी को खरी-खोटी सुनाना / डाँटना)

◦ Correct: ... will prevent her from giving him a piece of her mind.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "cake", "art" and "music" do not form any standard idiom in this structure.

NOTE

• Related idioms with "mind": "make up your mind" (decide), "on my mind" (worrying about), "speak your mind" (say frankly), "in two minds" (undecided).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Conscientous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Conscientous" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "conscientious", meaning careful, thorough and taking one's duties seriously. (कर्तव्यनिष्ठ / ईमानदार)

◦ Correct: She is a conscientious worker who never leaves a task incomplete.

• Spelling key: CON + SCI + EN + TIOUS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Committee" (a group of people), "Achieve" (to accomplish — remember "i before e" here) and "Necessary" (needed — one 'c', two 's') are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Commonly confused spellings: conscientious, conscious, conscience — all from the root "sci" (to know).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

The touch-sensitive surface is one of the reasons why tablets and smart phones are so smart. All touchscreens generate an electric field ______________ the screen. Your finger interferes with the field, and the device's operating system ______________ your touch or swipe.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. across; follows.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 1: A field is generated "across" (over the whole surface of) the screen — this is the natural collocation. (सतह के आर-पार / पर)

• Blank 2: The operating system "follows" (tracks/registers) your touch or swipe.

◦ Correct: ... generate an electric field across the screen ... the operating system follows your touch or swipe.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "past; attends", Option 3 "beyond; escorts" and Option 4 "onto; chases" give unnatural or illogical meanings — a field is not generated "past/beyond" a screen, and a system "escorts/chases" a touch makes no sense.

NOTE

• In cloze tests, choose the pair that fits both blanks logically and by collocation; a wrong word in either half rules the option out.

question:
Correct the underlined part of the sentence.

The rabbit runs fastly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fast.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fast" is one of those words that is both an adjective and an adverb; there is no word "fastly". So "runs fast" is correct.

◦ Correct: The rabbit runs fast.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fastest" (superlative) and Option 3 "faster" (comparative) need a comparison, which is absent here.

• Option 2 "as fast as" is incomplete without a second element of comparison.

NOTE

• Adjectives that double as adverbs without "-ly": fast, hard, late, early, straight, high. ("He works hard", not "hardly" — which means "scarcely").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The students were captivated by the __________ story told by their teacher.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. compelling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Compelling" means fascinating, gripping and holding one's attention. If the students were "captivated", the story must have been compelling. (मनोहर / रोचक)

◦ Correct: The students were captivated by the compelling story told by their teacher.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "superfluous" (unnecessary/excess), Option 3 "mundane" (dull/ordinary) and Option 4 "obsolete" (out of date) do not fit a story that "captivated" the listeners.

NOTE

• Synonyms of compelling: gripping, riveting, engrossing, captivating. Antonyms: boring, mundane, dull, uninteresting.

question: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Deliverence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Deliverence" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "deliverance", meaning the act of being set free or rescued. (मुक्ति / छुटकारा)

◦ Correct: They prayed for deliverance from the flood.

• Spelling key: DE + LIVER + ANCE (with an 'a', not an 'e').

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Banquet" (a formal feast), "Condescend" (to behave superiorly) and "Alliteration" (repetition of initial sounds) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• The suffix "-ance" (not "-ence") is used here: deliverance, guidance, assistance, appearance.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

He is reluctant to do the work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. hesitant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reluctant" means unwilling and hesitant to do something. Its closest synonym is "hesitant". (अनिच्छुक / हिचकिचाने वाला)

◦ Example: He was reluctant/hesitant to speak in front of the crowd.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "happy", Option 2 "disposed" (inclined/willing) and Option 4 "eager" are antonyms of reluctant.

NOTE

• Synonyms of reluctant: hesitant, unwilling, disinclined, loath. Antonyms: eager, willing, keen, ready.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: It is a obvious that child needs love and attention of parents.
option_2: It is an obvious that child needs love and attention of parents.
option_3: It is obvious that a child needs love and attention of parents.
option_4: It is the obvious that child needs love and attention of parents.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. It is obvious that a child needs love and attention of parents.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Obvious" is an adjective here (part of the structure "It is obvious that..."), so it takes no article before it. The countable singular noun "child" does need the article "a".

◦ Correct: It is obvious that a child needs love and attention of parents.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 wrongly place an article (a/an/the) before "obvious" and omit the necessary "a" before "child".

NOTE

• Structure "It is + adjective + that + clause" takes no article before the adjective (It is clear/obvious/true that...). A singular countable noun ("child") needs an article ("a child").

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

It's raining cats and dogs.
option_1: It's a perfect day for a picnic.
option_2: There are cats and dogs in the rain.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. It's raining very heavily.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to rain cats and dogs" means to rain very heavily / to pour down. (मूसलाधार बारिश होना)

◦ Example: We couldn't step out because it was raining cats and dogs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 take the idiom literally or reverse its meaning; idioms are not interpreted word for word.

NOTE

• Similar weather idioms: "coming down in buckets", "a cloudburst", "a downpour" — all mean very heavy rain.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

Ritesh remarked, "Honesty is a great virtue."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Wickedness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Virtue" means moral goodness; a good moral quality. Its antonym is "wickedness" (evil, immorality). (सद्गुण का विलोम — दुष्टता)

◦ Example: They were known for their virtue, not their wickedness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Probity", Option 2 "Rectitude" and Option 3 "Integrity" are all synonyms of virtue (uprightness/honesty), so they cannot be the antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of virtue: goodness, integrity, righteousness, probity, rectitude. Antonyms: wickedness, vice, evil, immorality.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word.

Improbable
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Implausible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Improbable" means not likely to be true or to happen; unlikely. Its closest meaning/synonym is "implausible" (not seeming reasonable or probable). (असंभावित / अविश्वसनीय)

◦ Example: It is improbable/implausible that he will finish the whole book in one night.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Plausible" (believable), Option 3 "Practical" and Option 4 "Tenable" (defensible/reasonable) are antonyms or unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of improbable: implausible, unlikely, doubtful, far-fetched. Antonyms: probable, plausible, likely, credible.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Maria was unhappy / because she terribly performed / in the examination / conducted last month.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. because she terribly performed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb of manner "terribly" should come after the verb it modifies, not before it. So it should be "performed terribly", not "terribly performed".

◦ Correct: Maria was unhappy because she performed terribly in the examination conducted last month.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The other segments — "Maria was unhappy", "in the examination" and "conducted last month" (past participle used as an adjective) — are all correct.

NOTE

• Adverbs of manner (well, badly, terribly, quickly) normally go after the main verb / after the object: "She sang beautifully", "He performed terribly".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A room in a hospital used especially for sunbathing or therapeutic exposure to light
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Solarium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "solarium" is a room (especially in a hospital) fitted with glass to allow sunbathing or therapeutic exposure to light. (धूप-स्नान कक्ष)

◦ Example: Patients recovering from illness were taken to the solarium for sunlight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sanatorium" (an establishment for treating chronic illness / convalescence), Option 3 "Planetarium" (a building for showing the night sky/stars) and Option 4 "Podium" (a raised platform) do not fit.

NOTE

• The root "sol-" means sun (solar, solarium). Other "-arium" words: aquarium (water animals), planetarium (planets), terrarium (small land animals/plants).

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

It is very hottest over here.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. hot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb "very" is used with the positive degree of an adjective, not the superlative. So "very hot" is correct, not "very hottest".

◦ Correct: It is very hot over here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hotter" (comparative) needs "than"; Option 4 "most hot" and Option 2 "more hot" are wrong forms — the correct comparative/superlative of "hot" are hotter/hottest, and neither is used with "very".

NOTE

• Use "very + positive degree" (very hot), "comparative + than" (hotter than), and "the + superlative" (the hottest). Never mix "very" with a superlative.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.

He spoke softly and ____________ (tensely), trying to diffuse the tense situation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. calmly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• We need the antonym of "tensely" (in a tense, nervous, strained manner). Its antonym is "calmly" (in a relaxed, composed manner), which also fits the sense "trying to diffuse the tense situation".

◦ Correct: He spoke softly and calmly, trying to diffuse the tense situation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "madly", Option 3 "furiously" and Option 4 "excitingly" are closer to synonyms of tension/agitation, so they would not "diffuse" the situation.

NOTE

• Synonyms of tensely: nervously, anxiously, edgily. Antonyms: calmly, coolly, serenely, composedly.

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank and make the sentence meaningful.

Anuradha travelled to Italy last summer and _____________________ the historic ruins of Rome.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. explored.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Explored" is the correctly spelt past tense of "explore", meaning travelled through and examined a place to discover it. (खोजबीन की / भ्रमण किया)

◦ Correct: Anuradha travelled to Italy last summer and explored the historic ruins of Rome.

• Spelling key: EX + PLORE + D.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "acsplored", "explord" and "explaured" are all misspellings with no meaning.

NOTE

• Related words: explore (verb), explorer (noun — a person), exploration (noun — the act). Note the base ends in "-lore".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As community-minded creatures who want (1)_________________ to belong, we often mirror others, including on social media, where we adopt phrasing, tone and expressions of emotion. In the past few years, social media has had a (2)________________ on hyper positivity: think cheery emojis and (3)____________________ quotes plastered over sunsets. Some put this 'good vibes only' trend down to the pandemic and a (4)______________ to avoid painful feelings when (5)____________________ on difficult realities. However, attempting to convey constant happiness is not only difficult but impossible.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. deeply.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank modifies the verb "want", so it needs an adverb conveying intensity. "deeply" (to a great degree / intensely) fits — "creatures who want deeply to belong". (गहराई से)

◦ Correct: As community-minded creatures who want deeply to belong ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "laudatory" (expressing praise) and Option 4 "crisply" do not describe how strongly one wants; Option 3 "abiotically" (relating to non-living things) is completely out of context.

NOTE

• "Deeply" collocates with strong feelings and desires: deeply want, deeply love, deeply concerned, deeply moved.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As community-minded creatures who want (1)_________________ to belong, we often mirror others, including on social media, where we adopt phrasing, tone and expressions of emotion. In the past few years, social media has had a (2)________________ on hyper positivity: think cheery emojis and (3)____________________ quotes plastered over sunsets. Some put this 'good vibes only' trend down to the pandemic and a (4)______________ to avoid painful feelings when (5)____________________ on difficult realities. However, attempting to convey constant happiness is not only difficult but impossible.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. focus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "a ______ on hyper positivity" needs a noun that goes with the preposition "on". "focus on" (concentration/emphasis on something) fits perfectly. (ध्यान केंद्रित करना)

◦ Correct: ... social media has had a focus on hyper positivity ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "blemish" (a flaw/mark), Option 2 "disregard" (ignoring) and Option 4 "dispersion" (scattering) neither collocate with "on" here nor suit the theme of emphasising positivity.

NOTE

• "Focus on" is a common collocation: "focus on studies", "a focus on quality". Here it means an emphasis on hyper-positivity.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As community-minded creatures who want (1)_________________ to belong, we often mirror others, including on social media, where we adopt phrasing, tone and expressions of emotion. In the past few years, social media has had a (2)________________ on hyper positivity: think cheery emojis and (3)____________________ quotes plastered over sunsets. Some put this 'good vibes only' trend down to the pandemic and a (4)______________ to avoid painful feelings when (5)____________________ on difficult realities. However, attempting to convey constant happiness is not only difficult but impossible.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. motivational.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank describes "quotes plastered over sunsets" in a "good vibes only" / hyper-positive context. "motivational quotes" (inspiring, encouraging quotes) fits this cheery, feel-good theme. (प्रेरक)

◦ Correct: ... think cheery emojis and motivational quotes plastered over sunsets.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "inobtrusive" (not noticeable), Option 2 "reticent" (reserved/silent) and Option 3 "deterring" (discouraging) contradict the upbeat, encouraging tone of the passage.

NOTE

• "Motivational" collocates with speaker, quote, poster, video — all meant to inspire and uplift.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As community-minded creatures who want (1)_________________ to belong, we often mirror others, including on social media, where we adopt phrasing, tone and expressions of emotion. In the past few years, social media has had a (2)________________ on hyper positivity: think cheery emojis and (3)____________________ quotes plastered over sunsets. Some put this 'good vibes only' trend down to the pandemic and a (4)______________ to avoid painful feelings when (5)____________________ on difficult realities. However, attempting to convey constant happiness is not only difficult but impossible.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. desire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "a ______ to avoid painful feelings" needs a noun that takes a to-infinitive and expresses a wish. "desire to avoid" (a strong wish to avoid) fits. (इच्छा)

◦ Correct: ... down to the pandemic and a desire to avoid painful feelings ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "listlessness", Option 3 "apathy" (lack of interest) and Option 4 "indolence" (laziness) express passivity, not an active wish "to avoid" something, and do not idiomatically take "to avoid".

NOTE

• "Desire to + verb" is a natural collocation: "a desire to succeed", "a desire to help".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As community-minded creatures who want (1)_________________ to belong, we often mirror others, including on social media, where we adopt phrasing, tone and expressions of emotion. In the past few years, social media has had a (2)________________ on hyper positivity: think cheery emojis and (3)____________________ quotes plastered over sunsets. Some put this 'good vibes only' trend down to the pandemic and a (4)______________ to avoid painful feelings when (5)____________________ on difficult realities. However, attempting to convey constant happiness is not only difficult but impossible.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ruminating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "______ on difficult realities" needs a verb meaning to think deeply. "ruminating on" means pondering/thinking deeply about something, which fits "difficult realities". (गहराई से विचार करना / मनन करना)

◦ Correct: ... to avoid painful feelings when ruminating on difficult realities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "laminating" (covering with a protective layer), Option 3 "collaborating" (working together) and Option 4 "stagnating" (becoming inactive) do not collocate with "on difficult realities" in the sense of reflecting.

NOTE

• "Ruminate on/over/about" = to reflect deeply. Synonyms: ponder, contemplate, mull over, meditate on.

question: Who among the following has written the famous novels (originally in Bangla) 'Devdas' and 'Parineeta'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Bengali (Bangla) novels "Devdas" and "Parineeta" were written by Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay (Sarat Chandra Chatterjee). (शरत चंद्र चट्टोपाध्याय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay is one of the most popular Bengali novelists; his other works include Srikanta, Charitraheen and Palli Samaj.

• Both Devdas and Parineeta have been adapted into several Hindi films.

NOTE

• Rabindranath Tagore wrote Gora, Gitanjali and Ghare Baire; Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote Anandamath (source of "Vande Mataram") and Durgeshnandini.

question: In which of the following states is shifting agriculture locally called Penda?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shifting cultivation (slash-and-burn agriculture) is known by different local names in different states. As per the key, in Andhra Pradesh it is locally called "Penda". (स्थानांतरी कृषि — पेंडा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Shifting cultivation local names: Jhum (North-East India), Podu/Penda (Andhra Pradesh, Odisha), Bewar/Dahiya (Madhya Pradesh), Kumari (Western Ghats), Ponam (Kerala), Kuruwa (Jharkhand).

• In this method, forest land is cleared and burnt, cultivated for a few years, then abandoned for the soil to recover.

NOTE

• Shifting cultivation is also called "slash-and-burn" farming and is common among tribal communities in hilly, forested regions.

question: Analgesic medicines are used for _________________.
option_2: correcting deficiencies due to vitamins and nutrients
option_4: killing or weakening microbes and infections
solution_text:
The correct answer is reducing pain and in fever.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Analgesics" are medicines used for reducing pain (and fever). They act as pain relievers. (दर्द-निवारक)

◦ Common examples: paracetamol, aspirin, ibuprofen.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 (killing/weakening microbes) describes antibiotics; Option 2 (correcting deficiencies) describes vitamin/mineral supplements; Option 1 refers to supportive/tonic medicines.

NOTE

• Drug categories: Analgesic (relieves pain), Antipyretic (reduces fever), Antibiotic (fights bacterial infection), Antiseptic (prevents infection on skin/wounds).

question: Who among the following was the captain of the Indian cricket team during the 1983 Cricket World Cup event?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kapil Dev.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kapil Dev captained the Indian cricket team that won the 1983 Cricket World Cup, defeating the West Indies in the final at Lord's, London — India's first World Cup title. (कपिल देव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mohinder Amarnath was adjudged Man of the Match in both the semi-final and the final of the 1983 World Cup.

• Kapil Dev's unbeaten 175 runs against Zimbabwe in that tournament is legendary.

NOTE

• India's other men's ODI World Cup win came in 2011 under captain M. S. Dhoni; the T20 World Cup was won in 2007 (Dhoni) and 2024 (Rohit Sharma).

question: Which of the following is NOT an important function of the Supreme Court?
option_1: It acts to check on executive authorities and enforce the rule of law
option_3: It maintains of land records and revenue collection
option_4: It is the protector and guarantor of fundamental rights
solution_text:
The correct answer is It maintains of land records and revenue collection.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Maintaining land records and revenue collection is NOT a function of the Supreme Court — it is an executive/administrative (revenue department) task. (भूमि अभिलेख व राजस्व संग्रह — उच्चतम न्यायालय का कार्य नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Supreme Court of India does: check executive authorities and enforce the rule of law, maintain federal equilibrium (settle Centre–State/inter-State disputes), and act as protector and guarantor of Fundamental Rights (Article 32).

• It is the highest court of appeal and the guardian of the Constitution.

NOTE

• The Supreme Court was established on 28 January 1950. Its jurisdiction is Original (Art. 131), Appellate and Advisory (Art. 143).

question: The Ebony, Mahogany, Cinchona etc. are trees found in which type of forests in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tropical Evergreen Forests.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Trees like Ebony, Mahogany and Cinchona are found in Tropical Evergreen (Rainforests), which grow in areas of very high rainfall (over 200 cm). (उष्णकटिबंधीय सदाबहार वन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Tropical evergreen forests are found in the Western Ghats, the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, and the North-East; they remain green all year as trees do not shed leaves together.

• Cinchona is the tree from which quinine (an anti-malarial drug) is obtained.

NOTE

• Forest types in India: Tropical Evergreen, Tropical Deciduous (Monsoon — Sal, Teak), Thorny/Desert, Montane (Deodar, Pine) and Mangrove/Tidal (Sundari).

question: Who was the first feudatory of Pallavas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vijayalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vijayalaya was the founder of the Imperial Chola dynasty and began his career as a feudatory (vassal) of the Pallavas. He captured Thanjavur (Tanjore) around 850 CE. (विजयालय — पल्लवों का सामंत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Vijayalaya built the temple of Nishumbhasudini (Durga) at Thanjavur.

• The later Cholas — Rajaraja I and Rajendra I — built a vast empire; Rajendra I earned the title "Gangaikonda Chola".

NOTE

• The Pallavas ruled from Kanchipuram; famous Pallava rulers include Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I (who built the Shore Temple and Rathas at Mahabalipuram).

question: All living organisms on the Earth are made up of carbon compounds. Many years ago, dead and buried plants started slowly modifying into coal under high temperature and high pressure. This process is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is carbonization.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The slow conversion of dead and buried plants (vegetation) into coal under high temperature and high pressure over millions of years is called "carbonization". (कार्बनीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Coal is called "black gold" but the *process* is carbonization, not "black gold formation".

• Peat is the first, lowest-carbon stage; the ranking of coal by carbon content is Peat → Lignite → Bituminous → Anthracite (highest carbon and best quality).

NOTE

• Coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels formed from ancient plant and animal remains; they are non-renewable sources of energy.

question: What kind of structures are generally used by Buddhists for containing remains of their monks and nuns?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stupas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stupas" are dome-shaped Buddhist structures built to contain relics/remains of the Buddha or Buddhist monks and nuns. (स्तूप)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The most famous is the Sanchi Stupa (Madhya Pradesh), built originally by Emperor Ashoka.

• A Vihara is a Buddhist monastery (residence for monks); a Chaitya is a prayer hall; "Garbhagriha" is the innermost sanctum of a Hindu temple.

NOTE

• Parts of a stupa: Anda (dome), Harmika (railing on top), Yashti/Chhatra (umbrella) and Medhi/Pradakshina path (circumambulation path).

question: Who among the following was the Viceroy of India during the announcement of the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Curzon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Partition of Bengal was announced in 1905 during the Viceroyalty of Lord Curzon and came into effect on 16 October 1905. (लॉर्ड कर्ज़न)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The partition sparked the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement; Bengal was reunited in 1911.

• Lord Curzon also passed the Indian Universities Act (1904) and set up the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in its modern form.

NOTE

• Lord Canning was the last Governor-General and first Viceroy (1858, after the 1857 Revolt); Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse.

question:
Consider the following lists and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List I (Congress Session)              List II (President)
1. Bombay, 1885                        (a) Rahimtullah M. Sayani
2. Calcutta, 1896                      (b) Rash Behari Ghosh
3. Surat, 1907                         (c) Sarojini Naidu
4. Kanpur, 1925                        (d) Womesh Chandra Bannerjee
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-d, 2-a, 3-b, 4-c.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct matching of Indian National Congress sessions with their presidents is:

◦ Bombay, 1885 → Womesh Chandra Bannerjee (d) — the first session and first President of the INC.

◦ Calcutta, 1896 → Rahimtullah M. Sayani (a).

◦ Surat, 1907 → Rash Behari Ghosh (b) — the session of the famous Surat Split.

◦ Kanpur, 1925 → Sarojini Naidu (c) — the first Indian woman President of the INC.

• Hence, 1-d, 2-a, 3-b, 4-c.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The INC was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume; its first session was held in Bombay.

• Sarojini Naidu, "the Nightingale of India", presided over the Kanpur session (1925).

NOTE

• Annie Besant was the first woman President of the INC (Calcutta, 1917); Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President (1925).

question: Jaiminiya and Kausitaki dances are mentioned in which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmanas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jaiminiya" and "Kausitaki" are names of Brahmanas — the prose texts attached to the Vedas that explain rituals and sacrifices. (ब्राह्मण ग्रंथ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Brahmanas are prose commentaries on Vedic hymns dealing with rituals, ceremonies and sacrifices.

• The Jaiminiya Brahmana is linked to the Samaveda, and the Kausitaki (Sankhayana) Brahmana to the Rigveda.

NOTE

• Vedic literature is layered as: Samhitas (hymns) → Brahmanas (rituals) → Aranyakas (forest texts) → Upanishads (philosophy).

question:
Match the columns.

List-I (South Indian King)             List-II (Dynasty)
1. Maravarman Sundara Pandyan          A) Hoysalas
2. Krishnadevaraya                     B) Chalukyas
3. Narasimha II                        C) Pandyas
4. Tailapa II                          D) Tuluvas
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-(C); 2-(D); 3-(A); 4-(B).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct matching of South Indian kings with their dynasties is:

◦ Maravarman Sundara Pandyan → Pandyas (C).

◦ Krishnadevaraya → Tuluvas (D) — the greatest ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire's Tuluva dynasty.

◦ Narasimha II → Hoysalas (A).

◦ Tailapa II → Chalukyas (B) — founder of the Western (Kalyani) Chalukya dynasty.

• Hence, 1-C, 2-D, 3-A, 4-B.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529) wrote the Telugu work Amuktamalyada; the traveller Domingo Paes visited his court.

• Tailapa II overthrew the Rashtrakutas to establish the Western Chalukyas at Kalyani.

NOTE

• The Hoysalas (capital Dwarasamudra/Halebidu) are famous for temples like the Chennakesava Temple at Belur and Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu.

question: Which of the following is considered as a day of mourning among the Muslim community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muharram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Muharram" is observed as a day/period of mourning, especially by Shia Muslims, in memory of the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (grandson of Prophet Muhammad) in the Battle of Karbala. (मुहर्रम — शोक का दिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Muharram is the first month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar; the 10th day is called Ashura.

• Bakri Eid (Eid-ul-Adha) — festival of sacrifice; Shab-e-Barat — night of forgiveness; Barah Wafat / Eid-e-Milad — Prophet Muhammad's birth anniversary.

NOTE

• The Islamic calendar is lunar, so its festivals shift by about 10–11 days earlier each year relative to the Gregorian calendar.

question: As per Planning Commission of India, in 2004–05, the percentage of total population of India below poverty line (Lakadawala Poverty Estimates combined) was:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 27.5%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Planning Commission of India, using the Lakdawala Committee methodology, the combined (rural + urban) percentage of India's population below the poverty line in 2004–05 was about 27.5%. (गरीबी रेखा से नीचे जनसंख्या — 27.5%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Lakdawala Committee (1993) estimated poverty using state-specific poverty lines based on calorie norms.

• Later committees: the Tendulkar Committee (2009) and the Rangarajan Committee (2014) revised the poverty-line methodology.

NOTE

• Poverty in India is now studied by the NITI Aayog (which replaced the Planning Commission in 2015) and through the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI).

question: Geeta Chandran received the Padma Shri in 2007 who is an acclaimed ________ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Geeta Chandran, awarded the Padma Shri in 2007, is an acclaimed Bharatanatyam dancer. (भरतनाट्यम नृत्यांगना — गीता चंद्रन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, one of the oldest, based on the Natya Shastra.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India (after Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan).

NOTE

• Eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (North), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (AP), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Who first postulated that cells are generated from pre-existing cells?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rudolf Virchow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rudolf Virchow (1855) first postulated that "Omnis cellula e cellula" — i.e., all cells arise from pre-existing cells. This extended the Cell Theory. (रुडोल्फ विर्चो)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Cell Theory was originally proposed by Matthias Schleiden (plants) and Theodor Schwann (animals) in 1838–39; Virchow added the idea that cells come only from other cells.

• William Harvey discovered blood circulation; Carl Linnaeus is the "Father of Taxonomy"; Jennifer Doudna is known for CRISPR gene-editing (Nobel 2020).

NOTE

• The cell was first discovered by Robert Hooke (1665); Anton van Leeuwenhoek first observed living cells (bacteria/protozoa).

question: Ustad Ghagge Khuda Baksh was associated with which of the following gharanas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agra gharana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Ghagge Khuda Baksh was associated with the Agra gharana of Hindustani classical music. He is credited with introducing the dhrupad style into the Agra gharana's khayal singing. (आगरा घराना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A "gharana" is a system of social and musical lineage/style in Indian classical music.

• The Agra gharana is known for its forceful, robust (dhrupad-influenced) khayal singing.

NOTE

• Major vocal gharanas: Gwalior (oldest khayal gharana), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala and Rampur-Sahaswan.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India lays down qualifications for the membership of the Parliament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 84.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 84 of the Constitution of India lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament (must be a citizen of India, of the prescribed minimum age, etc.). (अनुच्छेद 84)

◦ Rajya Sabha — minimum age 30 years; Lok Sabha — minimum age 25 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 80 — composition of the Rajya Sabha.

• Article 85 — sessions, prorogation and dissolution of Parliament.

• Article 105 — powers, privileges and immunities of Parliament and its members.

NOTE

• Corresponding article for State Legislatures: Article 173 lays down qualifications for membership of a State Legislature.

question: It is observed that a child's heart rate is 135 times per minute. The beat frequency of heart is ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.25 Hz.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Frequency (Hz) = number of beats per second. The heart beats 135 times per minute, and 1 minute = 60 seconds.

◦ Frequency = 135 ÷ 60 = 2.25 Hz. (आवृत्ति = 2.25 हर्ट्ज़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz); 1 Hz = 1 cycle/event per second.

• Time period (T) = 1/frequency = 1 ÷ 2.25 ≈ 0.44 seconds per beat.

NOTE

• A normal resting adult heart rate is about 72 beats per minute (≈ 1.2 Hz); children have a higher heart rate than adults.

question: What is the standard length of an Olympic-size swimming pool?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50 metres.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The standard length of an Olympic-size swimming pool is 50 metres (a "long course" pool). (ओलंपिक स्विमिंग पूल की लंबाई — 50 मीटर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• An Olympic pool is 50 m long, 25 m wide, with a minimum depth of about 2 m and usually 10 lanes (8 used for competition).

• A "short course" pool is 25 m long.

NOTE

• Swimming at the Olympics is governed by World Aquatics (formerly FINA). The four main strokes are freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly.

question: As per the National Multidimensional Poverty Index Report 2021, which of the following states has the least population under poverty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) Report 2021 by NITI Aayog, among the given options Sikkim had the least population living in multidimensional poverty. (राष्ट्रीय बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2021 — सिक्किम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India's first national MPI was released by NITI Aayog in 2021, based on NFHS-4 (2015–16) data.

• The MPI uses three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — across 12 indicators.

• Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh had the highest poverty; Kerala the lowest among all states.

NOTE

• The global MPI is published jointly by the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).

question: In October 2023, Raghubar Das has been appointed the Governor of which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In October 2023, Raghubar Das was appointed the Governor of Odisha. He is a former Chief Minister of Jharkhand. (ओडिशा के राज्यपाल — रघुबर दास)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A Governor is the constitutional head of a state, appointed by the President under Article 155 and holds office during the President's pleasure (Article 156).

• The minimum age to be a Governor is 35 years (Article 157).

NOTE

• The office of the Governor is dealt with in Articles 153–162 of the Constitution. The same person may be Governor of two or more states (Article 153).

question: In January 2023, the Warehouse Development Regulation Authority (WDRA) signed a memorandum of understanding with _________________ of India to help farmers get low interest rate loans.
solution_text:
The correct answer is State Bank of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2023, the Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA) signed an MoU with the State Bank of India (SBI) to help farmers obtain low-interest-rate loans against electronic Negotiable Warehouse Receipts (e-NWRs). (भारतीय स्टेट बैंक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• WDRA was established in 2010 under the Warehousing (Development and Regulation) Act, 2007, to regulate warehouses and the e-NWR system.

• Loans against e-NWRs allow farmers to store produce and get credit without distress-selling their crops.

NOTE

• The State Bank of India (SBI) is India's largest public-sector bank, headquartered in Mumbai; it was established in 1955 (from the Imperial Bank of India).

question: Recreation services are an example of _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is consumer goods.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Recreation services (entertainment, leisure, etc.) are consumed directly by people for the satisfaction of their wants, so they are classified as consumer goods (final goods/services). (उपभोक्ता वस्तुएँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Consumer goods — final goods used by consumers to satisfy wants directly (food, clothing, recreation).

• Capital goods — used to produce other goods (machines, tools); Intermediate goods — used up in producing final goods (raw materials); Inferior goods — goods whose demand falls as income rises.

NOTE

• In national income accounting, only final goods and services are counted to avoid double counting; intermediate goods are excluded.
